title: We will discuss two topics today. How do we detect device addiction among our families? And how can we help them recover from it? And then what are the latest online threats that are harming millions of people, especially children? What can we do to protect our loved ones from these harms?
agenda-journey: First, we will discuss the scale of the problem of device addiction and online harm, especially among the children population. Then understand what content creators and game developers do to make their stuff so addictive. What can we do to help our family recover from device addiction, the major harms that impact children, and what can we do to protect them from those harms
year-gone: There was a large study done on internet users to understand how much time people spend on average on social media and online video. People on average across countries and age groups spend more than 18 hours every single week just on social media and online video. That's 970 hours every year. [click] If you were to live 60 years, you would have spent one-fourth of your waking hours just on social media and online video. [click] Add Netflix, Amazon Prime, and other videos and TVs on top of it; you get one third of your lifetime looking at screens.

phones-everywhere: A common problem we have nowadays is, we use mobile phone right before we go to sleep. Or we watch TV, or work on computers right before we go to sleep.This has serious health consequences. There is a reason why modern people are unusually unhealthy compared to their previous generation, despite all the advancement in Medical Science.
screen-time-research: There are many researches done on thousands of people to understand how your sleep gets affected when you use device right before you go to sleep. It was found that those who use devices before going to sleep have poor quality sleep, interrupted sleep, and complex, stressful dreams. A whole night of sleep does not recharge them. The next day they feel fatigue, exhausted, poor memory, stress and irritability. The reason is that when you look at a white screen before you go to sleep, your melatonin hormone is suppressed by 50%. Melatonin is a hormone that triggers your body's natural recovery process when you sleep. It's also a powerful antioxidant. It repairs damage in your DNA in every cell of your body when you sleep. When you have that Melatonin 50% less night after night, no matter how long you sleep, your body does not recharge or repair all the damage it accumulates throughout the day. As a result over time you develop long-term health conditions.
couples-on-phones: Nowadays, we have another problem that husband wife don’t spend quality time with each other at night, instead they are on their phones. They fall asleep when they get exhausted scrolling through social media. This has even bigger problem than sleep problem. Relationships drift apart, interactions start becoming sour, eventually separation, and the kid in the middle pays the price.

why-intro: Let's understand what the game developers and content creators do to make their content so addictive.
dopamine-pathways:
There was a study published on the famous Nature journal, which is among many many studies. The study concluded that both drugs and device release dopamine, the happy chemical, in our brain. 
+ When you get a like on your social media post, or receive a message from someone on WhatsApp, or you reach a milestone on a game, your brain is releasing dopamine and making you happy. Naturally, brain wants more and more of this happy stimulation. So, it does what it needs to do to get more of it.  
+ this is the same reward loop that drugs like nicotine or cocaine creates in your brain. 
There are lots of other studies. I'm not going to show you all of those studies one by one, but this is something that's very well researched and documented.

treat-intro: So what do we do about it? Before any tool or setting, it starts with how we see it. Your child is the victim, not the culprit. Children are not born addicts: we let it happen, often with good intentions, like a phone at the table to get them to eat. Then two first steps: make their devices boring, black and white with the sound off, and choose their games carefully: which popular games to avoid, and what to give them instead.
child-is-victim:
First, you have to recognize that your child is the victim and they need your help. Sometimes I hear parents complain, "kids are always watching YouTube.”. kids are playing too much games. kids don't eat if I don't give any cartoon.

At first, parents might start with Islamic cartoons, or simple games. But, if that doesn’t paralyse their kids and their kids are still moving, then they will then go for stronger drug like the Baby Shark drug, Cocomelon drug, Spiderman drug. 
These strong drugs paralyzes the kids. Their eyes get wide open. Their mouth is also open. Now, all the parents have to do is, put the food inside their mouth. 

This is how we drug our kids because we have become so impatient parents.

If you are feeding your kids while they are busy with a device, you are causing two more harms to them. 
they are not enjoying the food taste because their brain is heavily overloaded by the stimulation form the device. They are hardly sensing the food in their mouth.
Their brain gets used to having food and all these stimulations from devices at the same time. If the stimulation is missing, they wouldn’t want to eat. This is one of the reason why kids become fussy eaters.
three-things: To curb the addiction, we need to tackle the three things that make a screen so stimulating. [click] One: fast motion content, rapid cuts and non-stop action. [click] Two: colour, bright saturated screens. [click] Three: sound, music loops and sound effects. Take these away and the device becomes boring, which is exactly what we want. Let’s see how.
gray-research: Does black and white really work? Researchers have tested it, and notice: every one of these studies was done on adults. This is a colourful feed, the way your phone looks today: bright images, red hearts, red badges, LIVE tags. Watch the thumb, it keeps flicking. [click] Now we switch the same phone to grayscale. Same apps, same content, but it is just less rewarding, and the thumb slows down. [click] Three studies measured it. Wickord and Quaiser-Pohl, 2023, Computers in Human Behavior Reports: habitual users, the people who scroll out of boredom or habit, dropped about one full hour a day. That is about 15 days a year. Holte and Ferraro, 2020, The Social Science Journal, college students: about 38 minutes a day, over 4 hours a week, mostly from social media and browsing. Grey notification badges and grey colours break the automatic reward loop. Dekker and colleagues, 2023, University of Amsterdam: a strict two-week trial with all kinds of users. Time dropped a modest 20 minutes a day, but people reported a lower urge to check notifications, less anxiety and a stronger sense of control. [click] So this is not just for kids. If grown adults, who know they are being studied, still scroll less in black and white, imagine the effect on a child. Turn it on for your kids, and turn it on for yourself. Next, let me show you how to make devices boring.
boring-devices-color: When kids look at their device full of colours they will have a lot of visual stimulation and they will get addicted to it. But if the device is turned black and white. Then there will be less stimulation less addiction. So you are giving your kids your phone or a tablet turn that phone or tablet into black-and-white mode. In fact you should also use your phone in a black-and-white mode. You will receive that your device addiction has gone down significantly after switching to a black-and-white model. There was a research done by Apple that they saw that when the notification colours were turned black and white people why not clicking on those notifications anymore as much as they used to do with the notification was colourful almost half clicks were coming on notification when not notification icon on black-and-white.

protect-intro: We have walked through the ravine: drugs, grooming and suicide. That is the darkest part of tonight. Now we cross the bridge. This part is practical: what you can do at home, starting tomorrow. Tech-free zones, what the first phone should be, the parental controls already on your child’s device, safe browsers, WhatsApp privacy settings, and a checklist you can take home.
tech-free-zones:
Make sure that there are no internet-connected devices in your kid's bedroom. 

You need to create tech free zones for your family.

When your kids have no device in their bedroom, they will be forced to THINK. This thinking will develop their mind. Thinking fosters their creativity. They will have no choice but to find creative ways to spend their time. They will READ. And reading will do wonders. Don’t take all these away from them by giving them a device in their bedroom. 

And family time. Yes I get it. After long day of work, you are tired. The last think you want is to deal with your kids, or worse, your spouse. You feel like running far away from them, have your own “ME TIME”. Some personal solitude. 
Trust me, this is far less painful than having a kid or a spouse, who have become a device maniac, have ruined their lives, and shamed your family. And you are frantically running around doing damage control.
slow-phones:
If you are giving your kids a phone, their first phone should be a dumb phone. Yes, their friends will laugh at them. They will feel embarrassed. They will cry. But after couple of days, their friends will move on, your kid will get used to it. Most importantly, you have just trained your kid to have a backbone, to have self-respect. They no longer associate their worth with some metal and plastic. 

If you have to give them smartphone, then don’t give them Samsung Galaxy S25. Give them Samsung Galaxy 5. 10 year old phones and tablet.
The slower the device is, the less addicted they will be to it. They will see social media app are slow. Games are slow. Latest violent bloody games are not working well. They will lose interest after a while.
And this technique applies to you as well. If you are suffering from device addiction, ditch your fast phone, get a slow phone. 

I bought my wife an $80 mobile phone, and my kid has a $70 second-hand iPhone. None of them find this phone attractive enough to spend hours using them, and that has saved them so many hours of their life. And Alhamdulillah, none of them have had any embarrassing situation from their peers. Nobody cares. We sometimes put unnecessary pressure on ourselves because of some imaginary peer pressure, that’s only in our head.
protection-threats: Before we look at the protections, here are the four big threats we need to guard against: harmful websites, haram images and videos in the browser, excessive time on social media, and harmful videos on YouTube. The next few slides tackle each one.
parental-controls: Before you buy anything, use what is already free on your child's device. Google Family Link for Android and Chromebook, Microsoft Family Safety for Windows and Xbox, and Apple Screen Time for iPhone, iPad and Mac. All three can block harmful websites in three ways. [click] One: automatically block adult sites. Family Link: Try to block explicit sites. Microsoft: Filter inappropriate websites and searches, which also forces SafeSearch on Bing. Apple: Limit Adult Websites. [click] Two: block specific sites you add yourself. Family Link: Manage sites, Blocked sites. Microsoft: Blocked sites, add a website. Apple: Apps and Websites, Blocked. [click] Three, the strictest: allow only the sites you approve, everything else is blocked. Best for young children. Caveat: Family Link filters only Chrome, Microsoft only Edge (it blocks other browsers), Apple covers Safari and most apps. No filter is perfect, which is why we need more layers.
parental-gaps: So why not just switch on "only allow approved sites" and be done? Because it is impractical. Every homework link, every school video, every login page, quran.com, Wikipedia, Google Docs, has to be approved by a parent first. The requests never stop, and parents give up and switch it back off. [click] And children find the holes fast: they open links inside other apps or another browser, change the clock or time zone to escape downtime, or delete and re-download an app to reset its limit. [click] Compare what the built-in tools can actually do. They only apply their own browser restrictions, each one only on its own company's devices, they do not block drugs, alcohol, gambling, anti-Islamic or pro-LGBT content, social media is all or nothing, almost no ad or tracker blocking, and they are easy to tamper with. [click] Kahf Guard works at the DNS level, so it covers every app and every browser, on Android, iOS, Windows, Mac and even your home router. It blocks drugs, alcohol, gambling, anti-Islamic and pro-LGBT content, it can block just Shorts and Reels instead of the whole app, filters ads and trackers system-wide, and has a forced cooldown and DNS lock so children cannot simply switch it off.
kahfguard-website: Kahf Guard: blocks harmful content on every device in the house. Here is what scholars say about it.
choose-browser: Not all browsers protect your family equally. Here is what each one blocks out of the box, with no extensions: invasive ads, cross-site trackers, cookies, fingerprinting, malware and phishing, bounce tracking, and anonymous Tor routing. Chrome, the most popular browser, blocks almost nothing by default. [click] Brave is the only one that ticks every box, so it is the browser we recommend installing on your children's devices.
browser-comparison: Privacy browsers like Brave stop ads and trackers, but none of the mainstream browsers protect children from what they actually see. Kahf Browser does: it hides inappropriate images, forces Safe Search and a safe YouTube, blocks ads and trackers, and blocks harmful sites. [click] Five out of five, against zero for Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari.
kid-google: Step 1: create a Google account for your child as a child account (Google asks "Create a Google Account... you will help manage this account until your child is 13"). Set the date of birth so the account is 11 years old, and set the location to Qatar. [click] To change the location later, open myaccount.google.com > Personal info while signed in as the child and set the home address to Doha. The date of birth can be changed from Family Link. [click] Step 2: sign in with this account on the TV (YouTube app) and on every shared computer at home. Google now treats whoever is watching as a child: Google Search results are sanitised, the YouTube feed becomes much cleaner, and the ads on YouTube and Google become far cleaner too. Pair it with "train YouTube what not to show" from the previous slide.
wa-privacy: WhatsApp > Settings > Privacy. Last seen & online: Nobody. Profile picture: My contacts. Status: only share with the people you choose. Groups: My contacts (strangers cannot add your child to groups). Read receipts: Off, so a groomer cannot see when messages were read.
safety-checklist: I have made an online safety checklist that will help you configure Google Search, Bing, YouTube, and Instagram, TikTok, and other social medias. It's a simple checklist that you can follow and configure all these apps and services that your family is using, and you can easily prevent 80% of the harm.
trends-intro: Finally, where things are heading. The research on teenage depression, self-harm and suicide since smartphones arrived. Then the one change you need to make at home, and the verse that reminds us whose responsibility this is. And then, the way home.
